assessment: Activation of NMDA receptors requires two co-agonists: Glutamate that binds to the GluN2 subunit and glycine/D-serine that binds to the GluN1 subunit. In the present manuscript, the authors address the interaction of D-serine, which is a less studied co-agonist than glycine, with the GluN1 and GluN2A subunits using molecular simulations as well as electrophysiology experiments. Surprisingly they find that D-serine interacts with the GluN2 subunit, further expanding our molecular understanding of NMDA receptor structure-function. This paper will be of interest to those who study NMDA receptors and ligand-gated ion channels in general.
